newsitem.title: UK: Mosaic buys Bolton Wanderers for 22 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Mosaic buys Bolton Wanderers for 22 mln stg.

text.p: Mosaic Investments Plc said on Wednesday it is to acquire first division soccer club Bolton Wanderers Football & Athletic Company in a recommended offer valuing the club at 22 million stg ($36.3 million).

The enlarged group -- to be renamed Burnden Leisure Plc -- plans to develop into a diverse sport and leisure development and management business. It has applied for a listing on the London Stock Exchange, with dealings expected to commence on April 29, 1997.

"The combination of Mosaic's cash and Bolton's business will create a group with a long established, core activity in professional football together with the new stadium which will enable the enlarged group to generate income from a broader range of leisure activities," Mosaic Investments' chairman David Williams said in a statement.
"A listing on the London Stock Exchange, with access to further funds from the market, will help facilitate the directors' ambitions for the club for the long term."
Under the terms of the offer 1,135 Mosaic shares will be offered for each Bolton share and 11,350 Mosaic shares for each special Bolton share.
Irrevocable undertakings to accept the offer have been received for 75.2 percent of ordinary Bolton shares and 83.6 percent of special ordinary Bolton shares.
Bolton Wanderers, one of the 12 founder members of the Football League in 1888, is currently top of the first division and well place to secure promotion to the lucrative Premier League.
